Website & Ecommerce Strategy

Technology That Works For You

A plan to turn crosstechz.co.za from an IT-repair brochure site into the same premium, dark, electric-blue technology retail experience customers already feel walking into the Randburg & Ferndale stores.

Prepared forCross Tech Systems
ScopeSite, brand, ecommerce & ops
StatusGallery shipped · strategy for review
00 — Recommendation

The short version

Four decisions drive everything below. Full reasoning for each is in its own section — this is the answer if you only read one box.

Platform
WooCommerceWordPress + PayFast, self-hosted on SA infrastructure
Payments
PayFastNo monthly fee, native WooCommerce plugin, EFT + card + Snapscan
Phase 1 build
R18,500+ ~R650/mo running costs — site, catalogue, WhatsApp, no cart yet
Time to launch
3–4 weeksPhase 1 only. Full store adds 5–7 weeks in Phase 2
01 — Sitemap

From 6 pages to a real retail structure

The current site is one long homepage. This groups content the way a customer actually searches — by what they need — while keeping everything on a fast, static Phase 1 build until the store goes live in Phase 2.

  • Home rebuilt

  • Request a Quote new form + WhatsApp

  • Reviews
  • Contact
  • Cart / Checkout Phase 2
  • My Account / Order Tracking Phase 2
  • Repair Ticket Status Lookup Phase 2
  • Loyalty / Rewards Phase 3

04 — Ecommerce Platform

WooCommerce vs. the lighter alternatives

Weighted for what you actually need: repair-ticket workflow, serial/warranty tracking, and South African payment rails — not just "can it sell a t-shirt."

PlatformMonthly costTransaction feeSA payment fitRepair tickets + inventoryScales to 2nd locationVerdict
WooCommerce + WordPress R150–R400
hosting only		 0%
platform takes no cut		 Native PayFast plugin Yes — via free/paid plugins (WP ERP, Service Booking, ATUM inventory) Yes — multi-location stock via ATUM or similar Recommended
Shopify Basic ~R700 2.9%+R2
or 5% via 3rd-party gateway		 PayFast via app, extra cost Limited — no native repair-ticket concept, needs paid apps stacking monthly fees Yes, but cost compounds with apps Backup option
Wix / Squarespace Commerce ~R450–650 0% + gateway fee PayFast not native, limited apps No — not built for service/repair businesses Weak — inventory tools are basic Not suitable
Snipcart on static site ~R0–300
+ hosting		 2%
min $10/mo		 No PayFast — Stripe/PayPal only No — cart bolt-on, no ops layer No Not suitable

Why it matters for you specifically: WooCommerce is the only option here that can run a repair-ticket workflow and per-item serial/warranty tracking inside the same system that runs the shop — everything else means stitching together a separate helpdesk tool.

05 — Payment Gateway

PayFast confirmed as the right default

Matches your stated preference — and it's the one with zero setup/monthly cost and a first-party WooCommerce plugin. Rates below are typical published rates; confirm current pricing directly with each provider before signing.

GatewaySetupMonthlyCard transactionEFT / Instant EFTWooCommerce integration
PayFast Free R0 2.9%–3.5% ~2% Official plugin
Yoco Free online
card machine from ~R1,699		 R0 2.6%–2.95% N/A Via 3rd-party plugin
Peach Payments Free–negotiated R0–enterprise tiers ~2.95% Available Via plugin, more setup

Practical note: Yoco's in-store card machine is worth keeping regardless — it's not competing with PayFast, it's your physical counter payment device. The recommendation above is specifically for the online store checkout.

06 — WhatsApp-First Journey

The site's job is to start the WhatsApp chat, not replace it

Every product page, service page and CTA funnels into WhatsApp Business — where an AI assistant handles the first 80% and a human takes over the moment it gets specific.

01

Customer browses

Sees a product or service page on the site, taps "WhatsApp Charles"

→
02

AI assistant replies

Answers stock, price, spec and basic repair questions instantly, 24/7

→
03

Quote or booking

Bot generates a quote or repair-booking slot, or asks for photos of the fault

→
04

Human handover

Anything price-sensitive, technical, or a complaint routes straight to Charles/staff

→
05

Order / repair updates

Automated status pings — "ready for collection," "part arrived" — no phone tag

①WhatsApp Business API

Official API (via a BSP like 360dialog or Twilio) — needed for automation beyond the free app, ~R400–900/mo depending on volume.

②AI chatbot layer

A lightweight flow (e.g. Wati, Zoko, or a custom bot on the same API) trained on your product list, prices, and repair FAQs.

③Human handover rule

Any message containing a complaint keyword, a negotiation, or 2+ unanswered bot replies pings a staff phone directly.

07 — Inventory System

One stock count, two sales channels

The failure mode to avoid: selling the same laptop in-store and online at the same time. A single source of truth fixes that.

In-store POS
Till sale deducts stock instantly
Central Inventory
WooCommerce + ATUM (or Sage Stock) — single quantity per SKU
Online store
Order deducts the same stock record

QtyProduct quantity

Per-SKU stock count, synced live between counter and website — no overselling.

S/NSerial numbers

Each unit (especially refurbished PCs/laptops) logged against its own serial for traceability and warranty claims.

WtyWarranty tracking

Purchase date + warranty term per serial, so a customer's cover status is a lookup, not a guess.

SupSupplier records

Cost price, supplier, and reorder point per SKU — flags what to restock before it's a gap.

CstCustomer history

Purchases and repair jobs tied to a customer profile — instant context when they call back.

08 — Bookkeeping

Let the store post the books itself

The point of integrating accounting software isn't the software — it's not re-typing every sale by hand at month-end.

ToolCostVAT (SARS)WooCommerce syncBest for
Sage Business Cloud Accounting ~R280/mo SA VAT201-ready Via Zapier / native connector SA-built, accountant-friendly, easiest handoff to a bookkeeper
Zoho Books ~R450/mo SA VAT supported Native WooCommerce integration Best if you also want Zoho Inventory/CRM in one suite
Xero ~R550/mo VAT via add-on Via plugin (WooCommerce sync) Strong if you plan to bring in an external accountant used to Xero

Whichever tool, the workflow is the same: every WooCommerce order and in-store POS sale posts as an invoice automatically, expenses get photographed and categorised via the mobile app, and inventory value updates alongside stock — so margin per product is always visible, not a quarterly guess.

09 — Cost Estimate

What each phase actually costs

One-time build cost plus what it costs to keep running, in South African Rand. Treat these as planning figures — get fixed quotes from your chosen developer/host before committing.

PhaseOne-time buildMonthly runningIncludes
1 · Site + WhatsApp R15,000–22,000 R550–750 Rebuilt site, catalogue (no cart), WhatsApp Business setup, hosting + domain
2 · Full ecommerce R25,000–40,000 R1,200–1,800 WooCommerce store, PayFast, ATUM inventory, repair-ticket system, bookkeeping sync
3 · Loyalty R8,000–14,000 +R250–400 Points/rewards plugin, customer accounts, referral tracking
4 · AI marketplace R40,000+ R2,000+ AI product recommendations, multi-vendor/supplier listings, advanced automation
10 — Implementation Roadmap

Four phases, each one shippable on its own

No phase depends on committing to the next one — you can stop after Phase 1 and still have a real upgrade.

PHASE 1

Site + Catalogue + WhatsApp

Weeks 1–4
  • Dark/electric-blue rebuild
  • Product & service catalogue (no cart)
  • WhatsApp Business + quote/booking forms
  • Local SEO foundation
PHASE 2

Full Ecommerce + Stock

Weeks 5–11
  • WooCommerce + PayFast checkout
  • Live inventory, in-store ↔ online sync
  • Repair-ticket system
  • Bookkeeping integration
PHASE 3

Loyalty System

Weeks 12–14
  • Points on purchases + repairs
  • Customer accounts & order history
  • Referral rewards
PHASE 4

AI Marketplace

Month 5+
  • AI product & upgrade recommendations
  • Supplier/marketplace listings
  • Predictive restock alerts
11 — Conversion Improvements

Small changes, most of them free

None of these need Phase 2. They're copy, layout and CTA fixes that apply to the site as it stands today.

1Four CTAs above the fold

WhatsApp Enquiry, Request a Quote, Book a Repair, Check Stock — currently only WhatsApp exists in the hero.

2Real photos everywhere

Gallery is done — extend the same real-photo treatment to service cards and the about section, replacing icon illustrations.

3Stock/price visibility

Even without a cart, showing "In Stock" / "From R4,499" on product cards removes the #1 reason people don't message.

4Two-location clarity

Randburg and Ferndale need their own address, hours and map pin — right now they're implied, not stated.

5Response-time promise

"We reply on WhatsApp in under 15 minutes, 7 days a week" — a concrete claim converts better than "contact us."

6Repair-status page

A simple "enter your ticket number" lookup cuts the single biggest repeat-contact reason: "is it ready yet?"

12 — SEO Strategy

Win "near me" before worrying about national rank

Two locations is an advantage most competitors don't have — each becomes its own local-search entry point.

GBPTwo Google Business Profiles

Separate, fully-completed profiles for Randburg and Ferndale — photos, hours, services, and review replies drive local pack ranking more than anything on-site.

SchStructured data

The site already has LocalBusiness JSON-LD — extend it with Product, Review and Service schema per page so listings can show price/rating in search.

PgOne page per service

"Laptop screen repair Randburg," "CCTV installation Ferndale" — each gets its own indexable page instead of one shared paragraph.

RevReview velocity

A WhatsApp auto-message after every completed repair/sale asking for a Google review, sent from the same flow as the order-ready ping.

ConContent that ranks itself

Short posts that answer real searches — "why is my laptop slow," "how much does a screen repair cost" — pull in people before they've decided who to buy from.

SpdPage speed

The current homepage embeds every image as base64, inflating it past 700KB before a single asset request. Phase 1 rebuild should serve images as real files.

Cross Tech Systems — Randburg · Ferndale — this report is a planning document; figures are indicative and should be reconfirmed with providers before signing anything.
